regulation: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013
title: United Kingdom: WEEE producer registration for electrical goods
summary: A producer placing electrical or electronic equipment on the UK market must register as a WEEE producer, generally through an approved compliance scheme. Flagged in v1; the full module is v2.

sources.title: The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
sources.note: Fetched the statute directly. 'Small producer' (reg. 2/2D) is defined as placing LESS THAN 5 tonnes of EEE on the market per compliance period (calendar year) -- confirmed threshold, distinct from the batteries row's 1-tonne figure in this same batch, so worth stating explicitly rather than leaving as a generic 'a threshold applies'. Reg. 15 requires small producers (or their authorised representative) to register directly with the appropriate authority; reg. 16 sets the application deadline (31 January, or within 28 days of first placing EEE on the market) and tonnage-evidence requirement; reg. 17 requires a producer who crosses 5 tonnes mid-year to notify within 28 days and join a compliance scheme instead. effective_from (2014-01-01) confirmed against reg. 1(2)'s own general commencement -- no date fix needed here, unlike the battery and toy rows in this batch.
